task1.title: Table and Pie Charts: Police Budget
task1.text: The table and pie charts illustrate financial information about the income and spendings of the police on a certain area of Britain for 2017 and 2018. The increase in budget was mainly because of rising in local taxes by 11.1 million pounds (from 91.2m to 102.3m). The incomes from national government, which was the major source in both years, and other sources like grants rose by 2.3m (from 175.5m to 177.8m) and 0.5m (from 38m to 38.5m), respectively. Spending on buildings and transport were 17% in both years. While the money was spent on technologic areas increased significantly from 8% to 14%, the finances for officers and staff's salaries dropped by 6%, from 75% to 69%. Overall, it is clear that while some sources of funding increased, a significant portion of the budget was allocated to salaries, despite a minor reduction, showing a shift towards technological investments over the two-year period. In summary, the financial structure of the police force in this specific region indicates a steady overall budget increase, primarily driven by localized tax contributions, whereas the spending distribution reflects a prioritization of modern equipment upgrades.

task1.title: Map: Norbiton City Transformation
task1.text: The given maps illustrate the transformation of an industrial site of Norbiton city to a residental area which is planned for future. Plus the houses, many new buildings will be constructed such as medical center and school. The medical center will be adjacent to the main square, while the school will be located at the east of the site. There will be built some new roads and a square too. Furthermore, new houses will be built at the farmland in the north of the river. This redevelopment project aims to completely revitalize the previously industrial zone, shifting the focus towards creating a habitable environment for residents. Alongside the housing developments, a variety of modern amenities will be introduced to support the growing population, ensuring that fundamental services are readily accessible. The restructuring of the road networks is also a key feature, which will improve navigation throughout the newly established residential zones. Ultimately, these planned modifications represent a major shift in the town’s infrastructure, prioritizing living spaces and community facilities over industrial operations for the coming years.

task1.title: Diagram: Life Cycle of Plastic Bottles
task1.text: The given diagram illustrates the life cycle of plastic bottles from the point that it is used to recycled in 9 steps. Overall, it is demonstrated that the process involve some hand job by individuals and machinery actions to manufacture new products from trash bottles. The procedure begins with throwing bottles away by consumers into the specefic cans for recycling. Following this, recycling trucks gather these wastes and transfer them to recycling center. Thereafter, blocks are crushed into smaller peices and washed to prepare for producing plastic pellets. Pellets are produced by an industrial machine and, subsequently, pellets are heated to form raw materials which used for manufacturing new products. End products consist of bottles, bags, pens and even T-shirts. All of these products can come back to this process as soon as someone used them and put them in a recycling can. By continuously repeating this cycle, the environmental impact of plastic waste is significantly reduced, promoting a more sustainable approach to material consumption and manufacturing in modern society.

task1.title: Diagram: Sugar Cane to Sugar
task1.text: The diagram illustrates the process of transforming sugar cane to sugar as a product. Overall, the procedure contains 7 steps, beginning with growing sugar canes and ending with drying and cooling sugar. Initially, sugar canes should grow about 12 to 18 months to prepare for harvesting. There are two ways for harvesting: mechanical and by hand. After harvesting, sugar canes are crushed to extract juice. Subsequently, the juice is purified by limestone filter and heated in an evaporator to become syrup. Once the syrup has been successfully formed, it is then subjected to a centrifuge process which separates the sugar crystals from the remaining liquid components. These crystals are further processed to ensure they meet quality standards for consumption. The final stages involve meticulously drying the sugar and then cooling it down before it is finally packaged and shipped to various markets for retail. This comprehensive process highlights the combination of agricultural patience and industrial efficiency required to produce a staple food item consumed globally on a daily basis.

task1.title: Bar Chart: Teachers by Gender
task1.text: The provided bar chart compares the percentages of male and female educators across varying levels of education in the year 2010. Also, the data demonstrates that the proportion of male and female teachers in secondary schools, colleges and private training institutions were roughly equal. Male teachers were under 10 percent in nursery/pre-school and primary schools versus approximately 95 percent of female teachers. The percentage of men and women were exactly equal at 50 percent in colleges and approximately 45 versus 55 and 55 versus 45 respectively in secondary schools and private training institutions. Overall, a clear trend emerges where female dominance is extremely pronounced in the earlier stages of childhood education, while gender parity becomes much more apparent as the level of education advances into secondary and tertiary phases. This stark contrast underscores the traditional gender roles that have historically influenced the teaching profession, particularly in foundational schooling, whereas higher education and vocational training sectors demonstrate a much more balanced distribution of male and female instructors.

task2.title: Opinion: Smartphones and Children
task2.text: In contemporary society, the ubiquitous presence of mobile technology has sparked intense debate regarding its impact on younger generations. There are many reasons for that such as accessibility and entertaining, and Overall, I think it could have negative effects on childrens. Smartphones are so attractive because they can use anywhere and anytime. Moreover, they offer many apps and games which is amuzing for a high range of young people. Therefore, they assign more time to these apps and games with their phones compared to other hobies. For example, schools offer online courses and homeworks which are accessible with smartphones. In addition, they decline parents conserns when their children go out with their friends because they can easily access to their location. On the other hand, there are many conserns about the significant rise of using digital devices like smartphones by childrens. Scientists say that spend too much time on watching limitless contents in social media has negative effects on brain in young ages. They prefer spend their time playing online games instead of physical games and sports. Consequently, this sedentary lifestyle can lead to severe health issues, including obesity and poor posture, which are becoming increasingly prevalent among today's youth. Furthermore, excessive screen time disrupts sleep patterns and diminishes academic performance, as students struggle to maintain focus during conventional classroom instruction. Thus, parents must strictly monitor smartphone usage to safeguard the mental and physical well-being of their offspring. In conclusion, while these devices provide undeniable conveniences for education and safety, the detrimental consequences of unregulated use far outweigh the benefits, requiring immediate intervention from guardians and educators alike.

task2.title: Discussion: Practical Skills vs Academic Knowledge
task2.text: Some people believe that, these days, practical skills are more important than academic knowledge in labour market, and in the future, employers may not request academic degrees from applicants. While the role of technical skills is getting more essential in workplace, workforces still need theoretical bases if they want to be promoted in their career. According to that, you can see many employees that are in the position unrelated to their academic majors, and even some of them have not any university degree. Academic courses give people fundamental information and basics of their professions. For example, if someone wants to be a programmer he can learn the skill from internet at least 6 months. But if he really wants to understand what happend in the background of an application and architecture of it, he needs theoretical background in computer science and it takes at least two years academic studies. Nevertheless, I think universities should change their programmes and put more practical courses in their educational plans to help students prepare better for job market. Without practical exposure, graduates frequently struggle to integrate into professional environments and fail to meet the immediate demands of their employers, highlighting a gap in the current educational paradigm. Consequently, a hybrid approach combining robust theory with hands-on internships provides the most resilient foundation for long-term career success. In conclusion, we can’t ignore the increasing importance of practical qualifications for professionals in job market and the fact that universities should adopt these trend and change their plans but there is still many benefits in academic courses for people who wants to advance in their career.
